To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ability to generalize learned knowledge to new contexts improves with age, and the generalization of learned knowledge becomes more broad as children grow older.
infants are able to transfer learned knowledge to novel situations, and that the ability to transfer knowledge develops over the first year of life.
8- and to a lesser extent 16-month-old infants are able to generalize learning from one situation to a novel, but related situation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of transfer of learning in infancy.
the development of the ability to transfer learning to new situations and how this ability develops with age.
the ability to learn and transfer learning across situations and across modalities during early childhood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of transfer is a complex phenomenon that involves the interaction of many factors, including the type of learning, the type of transfer, and the age of the learner.
transfer of learning is present from 8 months of age, and increases in breadth with development.
learning to transfer occurs during infancy, but the extent to which it occurs depends on the modality in question.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ability to transfer learning is a developmental achievement that emerges between 8 and l6 months of age.
transfer is modality dependent, with cross-modal transfer emerging later than within-modality transfer.
transfer of learning develops from within-modality to between-modality, and that this development occurs between 8 and12 months of age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
infants are not limited to transferring learned information within the same modality, but can also transfer information across modalities, with development.
